run.question:
EU prod is having a checkout incident — 500s on POST /api/checkout. Investigate
using the app-267-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The only log index present is app-267-prod-logs (green, 4 documents), and its documents carry cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1, i.e. they match the cluster this question names. Those four documents describe, between 2026-11-21T04:30:25Z and 06:00:25Z, a chain in which checkout-service returns 500s on POST /api/checkout because of a payment-provider (adyen-eu) response timeout, in which payment-service reports an upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms, in which checkout-service opens a circuit breaker for payment-service at a 36% failure rate, and in which payment-service acknowledges adyen-eu degraded mode with retry queue depth=620. That makes the external payment provider adyen-eu (declared upstream in payment-service's own error line) the deepest named origin and the checkout circuit breaker a consequence. Counter-evidence from the cluster itself is significant: in namespace otel-demo the checkout and payment pods are Running and ready, the payment pod's stdout shows Charge request received followed immediately by Transaction complete for every order from 04:25:26Z to 04:33:07Z, and the checkout pod's stdout shows PlaceOrder -> payment went through -> email sent without a single failure from 04:23:48Z through 06:30:32Z, i.e. during the same interval the index claims 500s; no adyen reference and no error line appears in either pod's stdout. All eleven flagd fault flags (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, etc.) are declared with defaultVariant off in the flagd-config ConfigMap, no NetworkPolicy-related refusal was observed (no policy objects were returned at all, which is unchecked rather than proven), and no K8s object in otel-demo shows OOMKilled, Evicted or probe-failure impact; the container restarts seen at ~04:23:42Z on nearly all pods (exit code 255, reason Unknown) predate the first logged error and their trigger is unknown. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for the whole Run, so the alert CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh could not be evaluated and no error-rate, latency or span evidence exists here; adyen-eu itself is not observable in the cluster. Conclusion is partial: the log-reported cause is an external provider timeout, the cluster workloads appear healthy, and the two log sources disagree.

claims.text: The registered Elasticsearch holds exactly one index, app-267-prod-logs (health green, 4 documents, 8kb), so all log evidence in this Run comes from those 4 documents.

All four documents in app-267-prod-logs inside the authorized window (earliest timestamp 2026-11-21T04:30:25Z, latest 2026-11-21T06:00:25Z) carry cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1, which matches the cluster named in the question.

At 2026-11-21T04:30:25Z the index records service=checkout-service, level=ERROR, message 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)', i.e. the reported 500 symptom with the payment provider named as the timed-out dependency.

At the same second 2026-11-21T04:30:25Z the index records service=payment-service, level=ERROR, message 'Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms', so payment-service's own error attributes the failure to the external endpoint adyen-eu /v68/payments.

At 2026-11-21T05:30:25Z the index records service=checkout-service, level=ERROR, message 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)', a checkout-side consequence of payment-service failures rather than an independent fault.
At 2026-11-21T06:00:25Z the index records service=payment-service, level=WARN, message 'adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620', the latest document in the window.

In namespace otel-demo the pods checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d are Running and ready with restartCount 1; both containers' last termination was at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 and reason 'Unknown', and both current instances started at 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z, i.e. the restart is in place on pods created 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z, not a rollout.

The 04:23:42Z container termination is not specific to checkout/payment: essentially every otel-demo pod reports restartCount 1 (kube-state-metrics 2, prometheus-readonly-proxy 3), and the prometheus-server container likewise last terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255, reason Unknown, restarting at 04:23:47Z; the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx restart at 04:24:05Z ended in exit code 1 with '[emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"'.

The single node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports Ready=True with lastTransitionTime 2026-11-20T16:32:02Z, kernelVersion 6.8.0-149-generic, kubeletVersion v1.37.0, so the 04:23 restarts were not accompanied by a node Ready transition inside the window.

The payment pod's own stdout for 04:25:26Z-04:33:07Z contains only successful charges: each 'Charge request received.' is immediately followed by 'Transaction complete.' with a transactionId (for example 04:25:26.705Z -> 04:25:26.727Z, 04:29:07.876Z -> 04:29:07.878Z), with no timeout, no error and no adyen reference.

A filtered read of the payment container's stdout over 04:00:00Z-06:30:34Z matching error|warn|fail|timeout|adyen|retry|queue|declin|unavailable|breaker returned only two informational Node warnings at 04:23:52Z ('MetadataLookupWarning ... incorrect Metadata-Flavor header'), i.e. no adyen or charge-failure lines.

The checkout pod's own stdout shows successful orders throughout 04:23:48Z-04:43:46Z (PlaceOrder -> 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' -> 'order confirmation email sent'), starting 04:23:48.802Z with its startup config using paymentSvcAddr:payment:8080.

The same checkout pod's stdout continues to show only successful orders up to 06:30:32Z (newest 200 of 662 lines, sampled 05:51:06Z-06:30:32Z, every order followed by 'payment went through' and an email), so the pod logged completed checkouts during the period when the index records circuit-breaker and provider-degradation errors.

The checkout Deployment configures no external provider endpoint (env PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, no adyen variable) and the payment Deployment exposes only PAYMENT_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd and OTEL_* variables, so no adyen-eu endpoint appears in either workload's configuration.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo declares fault flags whose names and descriptions target payment, including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%', variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable', on/off), with defaultVariant 'off' for both and for every other flag in the file; the workloads point at FLAGD_HOST=flagd.

Routing is intact: Service payment (selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment, port 8080) has endpoint 10.244.0.17 backed by pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, and Service checkout (selector opentelemetry.io/name=checkout) has endpoint 10.244.0.12 backed by pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n.

The grouped event listing for the authorized window contains only app-102b objects (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 1, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate 3, Pod Created/Pulled/Pulling/Scheduled/Started 3 each) and no event for otel-demo, so no K8s event evidence exists for the checkout/payment pods or for the 04:23 restarts.

The alert that frames this investigation is defined in the prometheus ConfigMap as CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh: the ratio of checkout SPAN_KIND_SERVER PlaceOrder spans with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR over all such spans in namespace otel-demo above 0.5 for 2m, labelled cluster=opspilot-m1 and opspilot_integration_id=m0-otel-20260909; its recorded 'alerts' value is '{}'.

flagd's retired container logged a graceful shutdown at 2026-11-21T04:07:51Z and its current instance started at 2026-11-21T04:23:49Z, watching ./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json and listening on 8013/8016; the retained flagd lines record no flag-variant change.

The prometheus-server container was alive and ingesting during the window, repeatedly logging 'Error on ingesting out-of-order exemplars' (for example 06:10:48Z through 06:29:49Z), so the missing metrics are a tool-path/logging issue rather than an absent Prometheus process.

The origin of the checkout 500s is the external payment provider adyen-eu: payment-service's own error line names an upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms, and a later WARN says adyen-eu is in degraded mode. This is a hypothesis only for the provider's own state, because adyen-eu is not observable here (no Deployment, Pod, Service or logs), so the timeouts cannot be verified from its side.

An alternative explanation for the disagreement between the index and the pod logs is that the documents' service identities (checkout-service, payment-service, external provider adyen-eu) belong to a different application/agent path than the otel-demo workloads named checkout and payment, whose stdout shows no failures; the index alone cannot settle this.

A flagd-injected payment fault during 04:30Z-06:00Z remains possible and unverified: the ConfigMap declares paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, but its defaults are off and flagd restarted at 04:23:49Z, so in-memory variant overrides in effect earlier cannot be read; no flag change is visible in the retained flagd lines.

Against any claim that the otel-demo checkout/payment path was failing during the window: both pods are ready, payment stdout shows completed charges 04:25:26Z-04:33:07Z and checkout stdout shows completed orders 04:23:48Z-04:43:46Z and 05:51:06Z-06:30:32Z, with no error lines and no adyen reference.

Resource exhaustion / OOM as the cause is rejected: no container's last termination reason is OOMKilled (checkout and payment both show exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown' at 04:23:42Z), both pods are Running and ready, and no Evicted, BackOff or Unhealthy event appears for otel-demo in the window.

Service/endpoint misconfiguration as the cause is rejected: the payment and checkout Services resolve to the running pods' IPs on port 8080, so checkout's configured payment:8080 target is backed by a ready pod.

An active flagd fault from the current flagd-config as the explanation of the observed errors is rejected as configured state: paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are declared with state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off', and no object is seen applying a change to the checkout or payment workloads.

Confirm the adyen-eu outage/degradation directly (provider status page, incident ticket, provider SLA timeline) and whether payment-service's timeout and retry-queue settings (30s timeout, retry queue depth 620) match its intended budget, since the provider is the only named upstream of the timeouts.

Restore the metrics/trace path used by the tooling (prometheus-readonly-proxy -> prometheus:9090, and jaeger-query) so the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule can be evaluated for 04:30Z-06:00Z and the 500 rate on POST /api/checkout can be measured instead of inferred from four log documents.

Establish who or what restarted nearly every otel-demo container at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (exit 255, reason Unknown; flagd shut down gracefully at 04:07:51Z) so that this change is either excluded from or linked to the incident; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

gaps: Prometheus metrics were unavailable for every attempt in this Run (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE around 06:31:00Z-06:32:37Z), so no error-rate, latency or alert-state evidence exists, even though the prometheus-server container was alive; the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert state at 04:30Z-06:00Z is unknown.

Jaeger traces were unavailable for every attempt (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there is no span-level evidence of error status, failure ratio or latency for checkout PlaceOrder or the payment charge call.

adyen-eu could not be observed: there is no Deployment, Pod, Service or log stream for it in acme-prod-eu-west-1, and its degraded state is asserted only by one log document citing its status page; whether the 30s timeouts originated at adyen-eu is unverified.

The frontend-proxy access log is not available (only 123 lifecycle lines, 04:23:48Z-04:39:58Z, and the newest line is a drain message), the load-generator pod had no retained log lines, and the frontend container had 12 lines, so the HTTP 500 rate on POST /api/checkout as seen by clients is unchecked.

The cause of the cluster-wide container restarts at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (exit code 255, reason Unknown on nearly all otel-demo pods; nginx exit 1 at 04:24:05Z with upstream prometheus:9090 unresolved) is unknown: no event exists for it in the authorized window, the node reports Ready since 2026-11-20T16:32:02Z, and the change_history integration is not available.

Whether a flagd fault flag was switched on during 04:30Z-06:00Z cannot be verified: no flagd management API access is available, the ConfigMap shows only file defaults, and flagd restarted at 04:23:49Z which would discard in-memory overrides.

Network-level checks are unchecked rather than excluded: the NetworkPolicy query returned no objects at all and the ResourceQuota query was not completed, so a policy or quota-based contribution cannot be assessed from an empty result.

The transient app-102b objects (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, 3 ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, 3 Pod Created/Scheduled/Started at 06:30:04Z-06:30:06Z) no longer exist as Deployments or Pods in that namespace; nothing ties them to checkout and they were left unchecked.
The app-267-prod-logs index holds only 4 documents, so log coverage for the incident window is extremely thin and an absence of a given message in that index is not evidence that it did not occur.
next_steps: Have the payment team pull the adyen-eu integration timeline (request ids for /v68/payments at 04:30Z, retry-queue depth trend) and confirm the provider's degraded window independently of the log line.
Once the metrics path is reachable, evaluate the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh expression and the checkout PlaceOrder span error ratio and p99 latency for 04:20Z-06:10Z to quantify the 500 rate.

Compare the four app-267-prod-logs documents with the checkout/payment pod stdout for the same seconds (especially 04:30:25Z) to determine whether the index documents come from a different agent or application path.
Review who or what performed the in-place container restarts at 04:23:42Z (kubelet/containerd event, deployment tooling) before attributing them to the checkout incident.
If a flagd-based fault is suspected, inspect flagd's variant-change history or management API and flagd's own metrics for paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable activations during the window.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
